clue.text: Fuss about drink — situation causing disapproval?

indicators.note: the word for fuss goes round the drink, so 'about' signals a container

parts.note: a fuss is an ado, as in 'much ado about nothing'
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone frowns on a commotion over alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: A RUM DO is British slang for a strange or suspicious business; the question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'rum do' is a peculiar, dubious affair, the kind of state of things that draws raised eyebrows.

clue.text: Fly low with courage

parts.note: blue means low in spirits, depressed
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: An insect flies close to the ground with bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebottle is a common blowfly with a metallic blue body, an example of a fly.

clue.text: Drink a very long time — one has several gallons

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink
an eon is an age, an immensely long period

explanation.surface: Drinking for ages, someone downs gallons.
explanation.definitionFit: A puncheon is a large cask holding many gallons of wine or beer.

clue.text: Pasquale given less than full assent? That's mean!

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so his name gives ME

indicators.note: the word for assent is not given complete: its final letter is lopped

parts.note: to assent is to agree

explanation.surface: The setter grumbles that a half-hearted yes is stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than full' trims the last E of AGREE to give AGRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre and mean are synonyms for scanty or ungenerous.

clue.text: Fails to pen four letters, maybe

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the word for fails holds the numeral

parts.note: misses means fails to hit
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone can't manage to write four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Missives are written messages, typically letters; 'maybe' flags that not every letter is one.

clue.text: Removal of a charitable offering presented without love

indicators.note: the offering is given with one letter left out

parts.note: an oblation is a gift offered to God or to charity
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A charity gift is handed over without affection and taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presented without love' sounds like a grudging donation, but love is tennis zero: dropping that O leaves BLATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablation is the surgical or erosive taking away of material.

clue.text: Struggle, having run aground crossing lake

indicators.note: the lake letter is placed across, inside the word for running aground

parts.note: a ship founders when it goes down or runs aground
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A boat struggles after hitting the bottom while crossing a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to thrash about or struggle clumsily.

clue.text: Irish house cleaner with no end of blarney

indicators.note: the cleaner's word is used lacking a letter

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day

indicators.note: the last letter of blarney is wanted

explanation.surface: An Irish cleaning woman who doesn't talk nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of blarney' removes Y, blarney's last letter, from DAILY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament.

clue.text: Student event with energy and passion

parts.note: rag is a British students' charity festival
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A student gathering full of vigour and enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage can mean intense feeling or passion, as in a burning fury.

clue.text: About original moon-lander, boy gets serious

indicators.note: the boy's word goes round the moon-lander's, a container

parts.note: a son is a boy
the LEM, Lunar Excursion Module, landed on the moon in 1969

explanation.surface: A boy turns grave thinking about the first lunar landing craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means grave or serious in manner.

clue.text: Attractive task for one on an errand?

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means charming or pretty

definitions.text: task for one on an errand?
definitions.meaning: going to get something and bring it back is what an errand-runner does

explanation.surface: A charming chore for a messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetching outfit is attractive; fetching is also the act of collecting and bringing back.

clue.text: Traitor mixed up with love in opera

indicators.note: mixed up says the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traitor caught up in a love affair in an operatic plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Il Trovatore is Verdi's opera of 1853, about a troubadour.

clue.text: Scot had one bairn, struggling without husband

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are thrown about and rearranged
the husband letter must be left out of the pool

explanation.surface: A Scottish woman with one child, struggling without a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without husband' takes H from HADONEBAIRN; 'struggling' rearranges ADONEBAIRN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aberdonian is a native of Aberdeen, so a Scot.

clue.text: Stickler getting on with the most celebrated people

parts.note: the on side in cricket is also called the leg side
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A pedant mingling with top celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A legalist sticks rigidly to the letter of rules, a stickler.

clue.text: Troubled and more like an invalid, it seems

definitions.meaning: troubled means worried or put out

definitions.text: more like an invalid, it seems
definitions.meaning: playfully, OTHER (more) put in BED, where an invalid lies

explanation.surface: Someone worried and sicker than before.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as B(OTHER)ED: 'other' in the sense of more, inside bed, the invalid's place.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothered means worried or disturbed, a direct synonym of troubled.

clue.text: Following pagan god, this writer has to be caustic

indicators.note: the writer's contraction comes after the god's name

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
the setter saying 'I have' gives I'VE

explanation.surface: After worshipping a pagan deity, the writer turns bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erosive wears substances away, as a caustic chemical does.

clue.text: Decidedly snide, nasty about Harrogate, say

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the town's word, a container
nasty suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged

parts.note: Harrogate is a Yorkshire spa town, an example of a spa

explanation.surface: A sharply spiteful remark about Harrogate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' looks like part of the insult but reorders to INDES; 'about' is the container signal, not 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In spades' is an idiom for emphatically or to a high degree.

clue.text: Fruit to set around throne?

indicators.note: the little word is set round the angel, a container

parts.note: taken as written
Thrones are one of the nine orders of angels, so a throne is an angel, hence the query

explanation.surface: Fruit placed around a royal seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throne' is no seat here: Thrones are an order in the medieval angelic hierarchy. 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo.

clue.text: Dad enthused about extra period of play

indicators.note: about here means in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Father gets excited about overtime in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden death is extra time where the first score wins.

clue.text: Artist showing a bit of chest

definitions.meaning: a chest of ... contains ..., sliding boxes

explanation.surface: A painter showing off part of his torso.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawer means a person who draws and also a sliding compartment of furniture.

clue.text: Prompt jet has cut time

indicators.note: the jet word loses a letter, which is cut out

parts.note: a spurt is a jet of liquid

explanation.surface: A rapid aircraft has reduced its flight time.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur is to urge on or prompt, as a rider does a horse.

clue.text: Page from mathematical demonstration that may go over one's head

definitions.text: that may go over one's head

indicators.note: the page letter is taken away from the demonstration's word

parts.note: a proof demonstrates a theorem

explanation.surface: A page of maths that is beyond one's understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go over one's head' suggests baffling, but means literally overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof is the covering literally above a person's head in a building.

clue.text: Self-consumed radical polemicist producing poisonous stuff

indicators.note: the name swallows part of itself, one letter shifting from inside to the front

parts.note: Tom Paine wrote the radical pamphlets Common Sense and Rights of Man

explanation.surface: An egotistical firebrand writer churns out something toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-consumed' moves the P of TOMPAINE to the front, as if the name ate its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaine is a foul compound formed in decaying protein, once blamed for food poisoning.

clue.text: Turned back when pierced by very good sword

indicators.note: the reversed word is stabbed through by the holy letters, a container
turned says the word for back is reversed

parts.note: rear means back
pi, short for pious, means very good

explanation.surface: Someone spun round as a blade went in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed sword for thrusting.

clue.text: Soldier runs, if pursued by old lover

indicators.note: the old lover comes after, in pursuit

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written
leman is an archaic word for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A soldier flees, as if chased by an ex.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifleman is an infantry soldier armed with a rifle.

clue.text: Ten awkward in accommodation for five

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the home word

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters sit wrongly and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Ten people crammed uncomfortably into lodgings meant for five.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentad is a group or set of five things.
